title: Every Polish group has a non-trivial topological group automorphism

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The title and abstract state 'Every Polish group has a non-trivial topological group automorphism' and 'every Polish group admits...', but Theorem 1.1 restricts to groups with more than two elements. The trivial group and the two-element group are Polish groups with only the identity automorphism, so the unqualified title/abstract claim is false and contradicts Theorem 1.1.

The abstract claims 'there are no uniquely homogeneous Polish groups' and Theorem 3.1 says 'A non-trivial Polish group cannot be uniquely homogeneous.' The two-point discrete group is a Polish group and is uniquely homogeneous: for any two points there is exactly one homeomorphism between them (identity or swap). Thus the statement is false unless 'non-trivial' is specifically defined to mean at least three elements, which is not done.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 1.1, extension of φ to H
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof defines H as the subgroup generated by Y and {x_i}, then says to take any non-trivial automorphism φ of span{x_i} and extend it by fixing Y. This requires Y∪{x_i} to be linearly independent, or at least requires φ to fix span(Y)∩span{x_i}. The paper only proves each individual t∈U\{0} is independent from {x_i}; it does not prove finite sums of elements of U avoid span{x_i}. This inference is false: in F2^4 with L=span{e1,e2}, U={0,e3,e4,e1+e2+e3+e4} satisfies the Lemma 2.3 conditions, but e3+e4+(e1+e2+e3+e4)=e1+e2∈L. Thus a maximal independent Y⊆U will have e1+e2∈span(Y), so Y∪L is dependent, and a non-trivial automorphism φ of L that does not fix e1+e2 cannot be extended by fixing Y. The construction is therefore not well-defined as written.
